self.disposition: 7-item checklist walked; 1 item failed and was fixed (Error Handling: EmptyLinkWalk escaped main() as Python exit 1, indistinguishable from a real hard finding -- now caught and mapped to exit 2 with JSON, pinned by test_the_empty_link_tripwire_exits_two_not_one). Item 7 (Affected Boundaries, ADR-024): producer = the gate's JSON stdout, consumers = CI log + p3.7's feeder; round-tripped 15x in-process plus once across a real subprocess boundary.

findings.finding: The plan explicitly changes the meaning of AC-1 from “behaviour-changing PR” to “PR changing spec criteria.” A code-only behaviour change with no AC edit passes untouched. This is acknowledged as Q1b, but it still means the proposed gate does not enforce the stated north-star condition.
findings.suggestion: Obtain an explicit change to the source acceptance criterion/scope that defines behaviour change as a spec-criteria change, or add a reliable code-to-AC signal. Do not present the implemented gate as enforcing behaviour-changing PRs generally.

findings.finding: AC identity rotation bypasses the greenness check. Changing `[AC01]` to `[AC02]` (optionally while editing the criterion), or moving a criterion between FRs, becomes `removed` + `added`; `added` deliberately does not require green bindings and `removed` is report-only. This can discard an existing AC-to-test obligation without triggering `binding_removed`, which only examines `changed` `(fr_id, ac_id)` pairs.
findings.suggestion: Treat an AC-ID replacement or relocation as a hard authoring violation unless the registry proves an approved migration, or match removed/added criteria by normalized text and route the old binding through the same retention/greenness checks. Add regression tests for marker replacement and cross-FR relocation.

findings.finding: The gate relies on `python-checks` remaining a required, PR-running check, but the plan only says this is true today. It does not verify that all merge paths use that job—particularly merge-queue/`merge_group` runs if enabled later—or establish ownership of the branch-protection contract.
findings.suggestion: Add a CI/branch-protection contract check or explicitly document and verify the supported merge events. If merge queue is used, run the gate for `merge_group` against the appropriate base/head refs.

findings.finding: The base-manifest-absent mode intentionally degrades to head-only bindings. On a long-lived branch whose base predates the manifest, a PR can remove a binding while editing its AC and receive only a warning, despite the plan identifying that as the exact disarming state.
findings.suggestion: Make this compatibility mode temporary and explicit: require rebasing onto a base containing the manifest for protected branches, or block changed ACs with head-side binding loss when `base_manifest_absent` is encountered.  Overall, the evaluator structure and fresh-CI-evidence design are sound, and the plan handles several subtle manifest and quantifier failures well. However, AC-ID replacement/movement is a practical bypass, and the declared spec-derived scope must be reconciled with the stated behavioural requirement before build.  SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise

findings.finding: The design says all three probes "must run and be reported before build is considered done". Probe A and Probe C are approximated synthetically in tests, but Probe B is entirely absent: no test drives `ac_criteria_digests` over the real `spec.md` at `545a4f320^`/`545a4f320` (verifying §2.2's measured 268-`added` shape), and no test exercises the base-manifest `git show` read at a real commit predating `.shipwright/compliance/test-traceability.json` — the very boundary the design's own self-review (§11 item 7(iii)) flags as "un-probed and the first place to look". All base-manifest tests use synthetic two-commit fixture repos; a real-git-history quirk (e.g. `git_blob_read` behaviour on an old tree shape) would not be caught.
findings.suggestion: Add a probe-B test (skippable if the pinned commits are absent) that performs both measurements against the real repo history, or record explicitly in the design that it was deferred with a card.  2. Retiring a requirement misreports as `binding_removed` with the wrong remedy

findings.finding: A PR that flips a requirement's `status` from `active` to `retired` in the manifest while also editing that FR's criterion text gets `head_links == 0` (the retired node is filtered out) with `base_links >= 1` → `binding_removed`, telling the author to "restore the `@covers` tag" — which still exists; the retirement zeroed the count. The outcome is fail-closed (blocks), so it is not a dodge, but the remedy is unactionable for the legitimate retire-an-FR flow.
findings.suggestion: When the head manifest contains a non-active node with the display id and an `acs` entry, emit a distinct "requirement retired while its criterion changed — retire the criterion and its binding together" finding instead of `binding_removed`.  3. `not_selected` is a catch-all for unexpected `executed` values

findings.finding: A link with `status == "enabled"` and any `executed` value other than `pass`/`fail` (e.g. `"error"`, `None`, a schema change to the field) is reported as `not_selected` ("this AC's binding names a test CI did not run — retag it"), which misroutes the operator when the actual cause is a failed/erroring execution or a manifest schema drift.
findings.suggestion: In the else-branch, name the actual observed value in the message (it does include `executed={executed!r}`, good) — consider splitting `fail`-adjacent values like `"error"` into the `failed` remedy. Low priority since it still blocks.  4. Duplicated `_run` / `_manifest_with_binding` helpers across two test modules

findings.finding: The CLI-harness (`_run`, `_manifest_with_binding`, `_edit_ac01`) is copy-pasted verbatim into the second module rather than moved to `_keystone_repo.py` — exactly the drift the fixture helper's own docstring says it exists to prevent. Not currently wrong, but the two copies can diverge silently.

The gate explicitly permits a PR that changes runtime behaviour but does not edit an acceptance criterion. It only computes a spec-text AC change set, whereas the stated AC requires every behaviour-changing PR to name its changed ACs.
findings.suggestion: Add a trustworthy behaviour-change/naming signal that covers code changes, or formally amend the governing specification to define behaviour change as spec-criterion changes only.

findings.finding: The required `ac_id → tests → last_verified_commit` baseline is deliberately not implemented. The diff has no persisted or validated `last_verified_commit` data, despite it being in the stated scope.
findings.suggestion: Implement and validate the baseline, or obtain a formal specification change removing that requirement before merging.

findings.finding: A valid-JSON but structurally malformed regenerated manifest can crash the gate: `_read_head_manifest` checks only that the top level is a dict, while `_links_for` unconditionally calls `.values()` on `requirements`. This produces an uncaught `AttributeError` (process exit 1, no JSON) instead of the specified exit 2 infrastructure verdict.
findings.suggestion: Validate `requirements` and the relevant nested manifest shapes before evaluation, and convert malformed structures to `ReadError`/exit 2 with a JSON payload.

findings.finding: “Probe A” does not exercise manifest regeneration; it directly overwrites the manifest with `write_manifest`. It would still pass if the actual regeneration step stopped overwriting the committed manifest or wrote evidence to a different location, leaving the hand-edit bypass undetected.
findings.suggestion: Add an integration probe that invokes the real regeneration/checker path with controlled JUnit input, then runs the gate against its produced manifest.  Block: the implementation deliberately narrows two stated core requirements, and it also has an unhandled malformed-manifest path. Those need resolution before this can be considered compliant.  SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: reject
